details.note: Spoofing: someone signs in as a member with a password reused from another site.
Passwords stored only as slow, salted hashes; failed attempts are counted here so accounts can lock.
Tampering: the borrow request is edited in the browser to push the due date out.
Denial of service: scripted searches tie up the catalogue during opening hours.
Information disclosure: what someone borrows is personal. A leaked export or a careless report reveals it.
Repudiation: a fine is waived and later nobody can say who did it or why.
Elevation of privilege: a member finds an admin page that's merely hidden, not protected.

name: Web app threat model
note: Walk the data flow element by element and ask which STRIDE threats apply: spoofing, tampering, repudiation, information disclosure, denial of service and elevation of privilege. Hang each threat under the element it targets with its mitigation beneath it, and look hardest at the flows that cross the trust boundary.
